root_idea.summary: The root denotes gathering things together into a compacted or accumulated store.
root_idea.development: Its lexical development extends from pressing or packing material into a receptacle to storing wealth as treasure, with related extensions to fullness, firm flesh, and figurative stores.

qac_form_accounting.reason: Displayed separately as the Quran-attested Form I verb.
Displayed separately as the Quran-attested noun.

senses.definition: To gather wealth and store it away; to hoard or lay it up.
senses.usage_conditions: In the Quran, used with wealth and property, including gold and silver, for retaining it as a stored accumulation.

senses.definition: A treasure or store of accumulated wealth or property.
senses.usage_conditions: The Quran uses it for substantial stored wealth or valuables, whether described as a treasure or as treasures in the plural.

senses.definition: A stored trove of knowledge or written learning.
senses.usage_conditions: In the Quranic account of the treasure beneath the wall, the term is interpreted as a deposit of knowledge or a written record rather than material gold or silver.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To bury property or treasure in the earth, or conceal it in secret.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A physical concealment specialization of storing property.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To press or pack a thing into a receptacle or the earth until it becomes compact.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Explicitly applied to dates and wheat as well as to things pressed by hand or foot.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To fill a bag or skin very full.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The containers specifically mentioned include a bag and a skin containing milk or water.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To stick a spear into the ground.
To become gathered, compacted, or full.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Applied in the cited usages to packed dates or wheat, compact flesh, and a bag or skin that has become full.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Property on which the portion due in alms has not been paid.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A technical or figurative usage reported in traditional religious usage.

other_classical_meanings.definition: An abundant accumulation of coveted property, especially gold and silver.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The term may be applied to property gathered together and desired as a valuable possession.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A repository or hiding place in which property is kept, guarded, or buried.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Here the noun denotes the place or container holding the property, rather than the property itself.
A rare poetic usage, reported as the only known instance of this meaning by the cited authority.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Figuratively, a stored-up reward or benefit reserved for its recipient.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of a reward kept in reserve, including reward in paradise; this is distinct from the Quranic knowledge interpretation.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The time or season when dates are packed, and sometimes when wheat is stored.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A temporal noun referring to the activity or season of packing.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Dates packed tightly in receptacles for winter.
One who takes extraordinary pains to hoard gold and silver.
Compact, firm, and abundant in flesh; well-fleshed.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used as a physical description of a body or flesh, including the cited animal, personal, and anatomical applications.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Richly stocked with useful contents, said of a book or writing.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative application of compactly gathered contents to written material.
